outline:
An embedded system is a computing system designed for a specific function or set of tasks and integrated into a device or product.
1. Design and implement a basic communication protocol (packet format, length, checksums, error handling, and retransmission strategy).
2. Use an RTOS (such as FreeRTOS or Zephyr) to establish multitasking, synchronization (Semaphore, Queue, Mutex), and time management.
3. Create a userspace program + systemd service + simple network communication (Socket, MQTT, HTTP) on an Embedded Linux platform.
4. Write modular firmware/system services on an MCU or Linux platform, implementing GPIO, timers, UART, I2C, SPI, ADC, and PWM.

Week 12 - Linux Kernel Compilation and Management
Week 13 - Linux Kernel Compilation and Management
Week 14 - Remote monitoring (simple web interface or CLI tool)

Week 18 - Embedded System Security (Flexible Learning)

category: 線上數位教材學習(Coursera、edX、磨課師等)(Online digital learning (Coursera, edX, MOOCs, etc.))
flexible_learning.content: The final six-hour course covers embedded systems security, focusing on key challenges and solutions. It includes an introduction to embedded systems security architecture. The next two hours will address major security threats like malware and data leakage. Participants will then learn about essential security measures, including authentication and encryption. The course concludes with practical exercises where participants design a secure embedded system and discuss real-world cases.
flexible_learning.outcome: To evaluate learning outcomes, the course will utilize various assessment methods. Classroom participation will be monitored to gauge engagement, while group discussions will foster knowledge sharing and critical thinking. Practical assessments will test participants' ability to apply their knowledge in designing secure systems. Finally, feedback will be collected to improve future iterations of the course, ensuring it meets the needs of all learners.
